hints.TestMarshalUsers: bs, err := json.Marshal(users); return string(bs), err. The struct tags in types.go already pick the JSON names.
hints.TestUnmarshalUsers: var users []User; err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &users). Note the &.
hints.TestSortSayings: for _, u := range users { sort.Strings(u.Sayings) }. u is a copy of the User, but its Sayings slice still shares the underlying array.
hints.TestSortByAge: sort.Slice(users, func(i, j int) bool { return users[i].Age < users[j].Age })
hints.TestSortByLast: Compare Last first; when Last is equal, compare First.
hints.TestBcrypt: bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(pw), bcrypt.MinCost) returns []byte, so convert it with string(...). Check: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(hash), []byte(pw)) == nil

quiz.q: Why would json.Marshal output {} for a struct with fields `first string; age int`?
Why must you pass &v to json.Unmarshal?
options: so Unmarshal can write into your variable
to avoid a copy for speed only
quiz.why: Pass by value: without a pointer, Unmarshal would fill a copy.

quiz.q: Which writes JSON straight to os.Stdout?
Two bcrypt hashes of the same password are...
options: different, because of a random salt
different only if the cost changes
quiz.why: Use CompareHashAndPassword to check a password.

quiz.q: The less func passed to sort.Slice returns...
options: true if element i should come before element j
quiz.why: sort.Slice uses a less(i, j int) bool func. (slices.SortFunc uses an int-returning cmp func.)
